text:
Maya R: thinking out loud — we need a per-org policy that protects us from sudden surges but doesn't grief bursty ML workloads. proposal: RPM + concurrency cap + short-lived burst credits. token-bucket style.
Samir K: token bucket + concurrency makes sense. fixed-window RPM will cause cliff edges during rollouts.
Maya R: yeah, fixed windows were the pain point in last spike. token-bucket with refill seems cleaner.
Leo T: +1 but note Dedicated customers will expect very predictable throughput. burst credits should be opt-in or bounded per contract.
Tess (eng-platform): UI question — how do we expose this in console? should be a single line: "quota remaining / burst credits" and a tooltip with refill rate. also need alerts when an org uses >80% of burst.
Ava S: agree on telemetry. metrics to surface: token_consumed, burst_used, throttle_count, concurrency_reached, avg_wait_time. we should track per-route as well.
Samir K: enforcement plane — where do we enforce? edge LB or router or runtime kernel? my vote: primary at router (fast reject) + runtime as final guard. edge could do a lightweight pre-check for known bad actors.
Maya R: router primary seems right. runtime enforcement is expensive but needed for last-mile correctness. edge-only would be too coarse.
Leo T: a note on behavior: when an org exceeds tokens, do we: 1) reject 429 immediately, 2) queue requests for short time, or 3) degrade to cheaper model? all have tradeoffs.
Maya R: prefer queue-with-timeout up to 200ms, then fallback to degrade model if configured, else 429. avoids sudden UX cliffs.
Tess (eng-platform): console UX: add a per-org "surge settings" panel: toggle fallback model, max-queue-ms, burst-window-size. also show historical burst events.
Ava S: for rollout plan: feature-flagged "org-rate-v2": 1% orgs -> 10% -> 25% -> 100%. increment only after evaluating throttle_count and latency.
Samir K: prototype enforcement middleware this week. rough config idea:
```yaml
rate_policy:
  rpm: 1200            # requests per minute (soft target)
  concurrent: 8        # max in-flight requests per org
  burst_credits: 240   # tokens usable above rpm for short bursts
  refill_rate: 4/s     # how burst credits refill
  algorithm: token_bucket
  queue_ms: 200        # how long to queue before rejecting
  fallback_model: small-1b
```
Maya R: nice. keep the names generic for console.
Leo T: telemetry retention — keep burst events for 90 days for audit and billing disputes.
Ava S: migration considerations: existing customers today using our old per-key quotas. We should map old quota -> new policy with a conservative burst conversion and email customers with recommended settings.
Tess (eng-platform): I can mock the panel and a flyout that shows "expected cost impact" when you enable burst.
Samir K: also need a lightweight simulator tool to run against a replay of traces so we can estimate throttle rates for a given policy. I can add a simple harness.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/ratelimit-v2 -> env=staging, status: success :white_check_mark:
Maya R: next steps: Samir prototype enforcement middleware + harness, Tess console mock, Ava migration plan draft, metrics dashboard prototype (burst/queue/throttles). I'll own rollout schedule.
Ava S: ping me once mocks are ready, I'll prepare comms.
Leo T: small nit — ensure Dedicated contract overrides are honored at router level, not just console.
Samir K: noted. will add a contract-layer check before applying default policy.
Maya R: ok, let's aim for a staging test with 5 synthetic org traces next Wed. :thumbsup:
__notes: single-thread Slack format; messages are short/informal and include code block, emoji, and a bot line
